title: UID 0 Restricted to the Root Account
description: Detect entries in the local account file /etc/passwd, as committed in the snapshot, other than the single root entry, that are assigned UID 0. The conclusion is scoped to that file.
collection_requirements: STANDARD_AUDIT: /etc/passwd is world-readable; a Standard Audit collects it | the route is necessary, not sufficient; evidence is sufficient when: | sources["etc/passwd"].status is COLLECTED (the per-source status; group and shadow are not required facts, so the section's combined collection_status is not used) | remote_identity_inclusion.via_compat_directives_in does not list etc/passwd | every local passwd record carries a numeric UID and exact name bytes
applicability: Every Linux host: the local passwd file is a universal source, and the condition does not depend on the host's role or purpose (IQ-070 does not apply). This criterion never yields NOT_APPLICABLE.
result_meanings: NOT_EVALUATED: the evidence is not sufficient (above). This includes PARTIAL, ERROR, NOT_TESTED, truncated or malformed passwd evidence, and a passwd domain widened by an INCLUDE directive. An additional UID-0 record observed in insufficient evidence is reported as an observed fact beside the result, never as FAIL. | PASS: the evidence is sufficient and exactly one local passwd record has UID 0, and its name is exactly the bytes of "root" (726f6f74). | FAIL: the evidence is sufficient and the PASS condition does not hold: a UID-0 record whose name is not exactly "root", more than one UID-0 record (including a duplicate root line), or no UID-0 record. | never produced: NOT_APPLICABLE, MANUAL_REVIEW
limitations: Only /etc/passwd is evaluated. A PASS means that, in /etc/passwd as committed, root is the only entry with UID 0. It does not establish that no other UID-0 identity exists: identities from other NSS services (LDAP and other directory services, SSSD, NIS maps), containers, user namespaces or any other identity source are not observed and are not covered. | Whether NSS consults the local file is reported beside the result (nss_file_effectiveness) and does not change it. | The criterion concerns account entries, not processes: a process running as UID 0 is not observed here. | Names are compared as exact bytes; a look-alike name is not root.

title: Empty Local Shadow Password Fields
description: Detect Empty Local Shadow Password Fields: local accounts whose /etc/shadow password field, as committed, is empty and not locked. The conclusion is an observation of that field only.
collection_requirements: FULL_AUDIT: /etc/shadow is collected only by a Full Audit (read_shadow_v1) | the route is necessary, not sufficient; evidence is sufficient when: | sources["etc/passwd"].status and sources["etc/shadow"].status are COLLECTED | remote_identity_inclusion.via_compat_directives_in lists neither etc/passwd nor etc/shadow | every local account's shadow relation is PRESENT
applicability: Every Linux host with local accounts. Role-independent. This criterion never yields NOT_APPLICABLE.
result_meanings: NOT_EVALUATED: the evidence is not sufficient (above). An account whose shadow relation is ABSENT_FROM_COLLECTED_SOURCE is NOT_EVALUATED, because the field the system then consults is the /etc/passwd password field, which the committed evidence does not carry (IQ-077). An empty unlocked field seen in insufficient evidence is reported as an observation, never as FAIL. | FAIL: the evidence is sufficient and at least one account's shadow password state has content EMPTY and lock_prefix LOCK_PREFIX_ABSENT. | PASS: the evidence is sufficient and no account's shadow password state has content EMPTY with lock_prefix LOCK_PREFIX_ABSENT. A locked field (leading '!') and the DISABLED_TOKEN ('*') are not empty fields. | never produced: NOT_APPLICABLE, MANUAL_REVIEW
limitations: The conclusion concerns the /etc/shadow password field as committed. It does not establish whether a login without a password is possible: PAM and SSH configuration are not evaluated here. | The /etc/passwd password field is not in the committed evidence (IQ-077); an account without a shadow record is therefore not evaluated. | No password, hash or salt is stored or shown; only the redacted state the collector records. | Only the local account files are evaluated. Identities from other NSS services (LDAP and other directory services, SSSD, NIS maps), containers or user namespaces are not observed and are not covered.

title: Duplicate Local UIDs
description: Detect Duplicate Local UIDs: two or more different local account names in /etc/passwd, as committed, that share one UID. The conclusion is scoped to that file.
collection_requirements: STANDARD_AUDIT: /etc/passwd is world-readable; a Standard Audit collects it | the route is necessary, not sufficient; evidence is sufficient when: | sources["etc/passwd"].status is COLLECTED | remote_identity_inclusion.via_compat_directives_in does not list etc/passwd | every local passwd record carries a numeric UID and exact name bytes
applicability: Every Linux host. Role-independent. This criterion never yields NOT_APPLICABLE.
result_meanings: NOT_EVALUATED: the evidence is not sufficient (above). A duplicate seen in insufficient evidence is reported as an observation, never as FAIL. | FAIL: the evidence is sufficient and two or more records with different exact name bytes have the same UID. | MANUAL_REVIEW: the evidence is sufficient, no two different names share a UID, but one name appears on more than one line with different UIDs: which line the system resolves is a judgement this criterion does not make, so the lines are listed for a person to decide. Repeated lines of one name with the same UID are listed as an observation and do not change the result. | PASS: the evidence is sufficient and every UID belongs to exactly one name. | never produced: NOT_APPLICABLE
limitations: Only /etc/passwd is evaluated. A PASS means that, in /etc/passwd as committed, every UID belongs to one name; UIDs from other identity sources are not observed. | UID 0 shared by root and another name is also reported by ISE-ACCOUNT-001. | Only the local account files are evaluated. Identities from other NSS services (LDAP and other directory services, SSSD, NIS maps), containers or user namespaces are not observed and are not covered.

title: Legacy MD5 Password Hash Schemes
description: Detect Legacy MD5 Password Hash Schemes: local /etc/shadow entries, as committed, whose stored hash uses an MD5-based scheme (MD5_CRYPT or SUN_MD5). The conclusion concerns the stored scheme only.
collection_requirements: FULL_AUDIT: /etc/shadow is collected only by a Full Audit (read_shadow_v1) | the route is necessary, not sufficient; evidence is sufficient when: | sources["etc/passwd"].status and sources["etc/shadow"].status are COLLECTED | remote_identity_inclusion.via_compat_directives_in lists neither etc/passwd nor etc/shadow
applicability: Every Linux host with local accounts. Role-independent. This criterion never yields NOT_APPLICABLE.
result_meanings: NOT_EVALUATED: the evidence is not sufficient (above); or no MD5 scheme is seen but some state cannot be classified: content OTHER, hash_scheme OTHER_RECOGNIZED_FORMAT, an account whose shadow relation is not PRESENT, or an orphan shadow record, whose state is not recorded. OTHER is never read as safe and never as DES. | FAIL: the evidence is sufficient and at least one shadow password state has content HASH_PRESENT and hash_scheme MD5_CRYPT or SUN_MD5, locked or not. | PASS: the evidence is sufficient, every account has a PRESENT shadow record, there is no orphan shadow record, and every HASH_PRESENT state names one of BCRYPT, SHA256_CRYPT, SHA512_CRYPT, SCRYPT, YESCRYPT or GOST_YESCRYPT. EMPTY and DISABLED_TOKEN fields carry no hash and do not affect this criterion. | never produced: NOT_APPLICABLE, MANUAL_REVIEW
limitations: Only MD5_CRYPT and SUN_MD5 are detected. Traditional DES crypt has no recognised prefix and is recorded as content OTHER, which gives NOT_EVALUATED, not FAIL (IQ-075). | The scheme of the stored hash is evaluated, not the policy for new passwords; a FAIL does not claim that the account can log in. | No password, hash or salt is stored or shown; only the bounded scheme name the collector records. | Only the local account files are evaluated. Identities from other NSS services (LDAP and other directory services, SSSD, NIS maps), containers or user namespaces are not observed and are not covered.

title: SSH Global PermitEmptyPasswords Configuration
description: SSH Global PermitEmptyPasswords Configuration: the global value of PermitEmptyPasswords that sshd -T reports, as committed. The conclusion concerns the global configuration only, not every connection.
collection_requirements: FULL_AUDIT: sshd -T is run only by a Full Audit (resolve_sshd_effective_config_v1) | the route is necessary, not sufficient; evidence is sufficient when: | the one coverage entry whose operation_id is resolve_sshd_effective_config_v1 has status COLLECTED | exactly one RESOLVED_SETTING record has keyword permitemptypasswords
applicability: Hosts where the Full Audit could run sshd -T. Role-independent. This criterion never yields NOT_APPLICABLE: an sshd absent at the fixed path /usr/sbin/sshd does not prove that no SSH server exists.
result_meanings: NOT_EVALUATED: the resolved dimension is not COLLECTED (including TOOL_ABSENT, a refused or failed sshd -T, and every Standard Audit), or the setting is not reported exactly once. The reason names the coverage status. | PASS: the evidence is sufficient and the value is no. The result concerns the global configuration. | FAIL: the evidence is sufficient and the value is yes. | NOT_EVALUATED: the evidence is sufficient but the value is neither yes nor no. | never produced: NOT_APPLICABLE, MANUAL_REVIEW
limitations: sshd -T is run without a connection context, so Match blocks are not applied. A global no does not establish that every connection refuses empty passwords; Match-scoped PermitEmptyPasswords declarations are listed as observations and never change the result. | Only the sshd at /usr/sbin/sshd is observed; another SSH server (another path, a different implementation) is not. | Whether any account has an empty password is ISE-ACCOUNT-002, not this criterion.

title: Duplicate Local GIDs
description: Detect Duplicate Local GIDs: two or more different group names in /etc/group, as committed, that share one GID. The conclusion is scoped to that file.
collection_requirements: STANDARD_AUDIT: /etc/group is world-readable; a Standard Audit collects it | the route is necessary, not sufficient; evidence is sufficient when: | sources["etc/group"].status is COLLECTED | remote_identity_inclusion.via_compat_directives_in does not list etc/group | every local group record carries a numeric GID and exact name bytes
applicability: Every Linux host. Role-independent. This criterion never yields NOT_APPLICABLE.
result_meanings: NOT_EVALUATED: the evidence is not sufficient (above). A duplicate seen in insufficient evidence is reported as an observation, never as FAIL. | FAIL: the evidence is sufficient and two or more records with different exact name bytes have the same GID. | MANUAL_REVIEW: the evidence is sufficient, no two different names share a GID, but one name appears on more than one line with different GIDs, both lines kept in the evidence: which line the system resolves needs a person. Repeated identical entries are listed as observations and do not change the result. | PASS: the evidence is sufficient and every GID belongs to exactly one name. | never produced: NOT_APPLICABLE
limitations: Only /etc/group is evaluated. A PASS means that, in /etc/group as committed, every GID belongs to one name; groups from LDAP, SSSD, NIS or other NSS services are not observed. | A shared GID is an identity and accountability problem; on its own it is not evidence of a privilege escalation. | Group membership and group passwords are not evaluated.

title: Declared login.defs Password Hashing Method
description: Declared login.defs Password Hashing Method: evaluate the ENCRYPT_METHOD value declared in /etc/login.defs, as committed, against a narrowly defined legacy-algorithm policy (MD5 and DES are legacy), without claiming the effective PAM password hashing behaviour.
collection_requirements: STANDARD_AUDIT: /etc/login.defs is world-readable; a Standard Audit collects it | the route is necessary, not sufficient; evidence is sufficient when: | every provenance source of family LOGIN_DEFS has status COLLECTED | exactly one well-formed ENCRYPT_METHOD record of family LOGIN_DEFS exists, with retention RETAIN_VALUE
applicability: Every Linux host with /etc/login.defs. Role-independent. This criterion never yields NOT_APPLICABLE.
result_meanings: NOT_EVALUATED: the evidence is not sufficient: a LOGIN_DEFS source not COLLECTED, no ENCRYPT_METHOD declared (the built-in default differs between distributions), more than one ENCRYPT_METHOD (conflicting), a malformed record, or a value not retained. | FAIL: the evidence is sufficient and the value is exactly MD5 or DES. | PASS: the evidence is sufficient and the value is exactly SHA256 or SHA512: the declared method is not a legacy one. This is not a claim that the system as a whole uses a secure password hashing policy. | NOT_EVALUATED: the value is YESCRYPT or BCRYPT, whose support depends on the shadow-utils and libxcrypt build of the platform, which the committed evidence does not record; or any other value, including a known method spelled in another case, which never passes. | never produced: NOT_APPLICABLE, MANUAL_REVIEW
limitations: The criterion evaluates the declared login.defs setting only. pam_unix options, other tools and distribution defaults decide the method actually applied when a password is changed; they are not evaluated. | A PASS does not mean that the system uses a secure password hashing policy, only that the declared ENCRYPT_METHOD is not MD5 or DES. | YESCRYPT and BCRYPT give NOT_EVALUATED: platform support for them is not in the committed evidence.

title: Global SSH StrictModes Configuration
description: Global SSH StrictModes Configuration: the global value of StrictModes that sshd -T reports, as committed. The conclusion concerns the global configuration only.
collection_requirements: FULL_AUDIT: sshd -T is run only by a Full Audit (resolve_sshd_effective_config_v1) | the route is necessary, not sufficient; evidence is sufficient when: | the one coverage entry whose operation_id is resolve_sshd_effective_config_v1 has status COLLECTED | exactly one RESOLVED_SETTING record has keyword strictmodes
applicability: Hosts where the Full Audit could run sshd -T. Role-independent. This criterion never yields NOT_APPLICABLE: an sshd absent at /usr/sbin/sshd does not prove that no SSH server exists.
result_meanings: NOT_EVALUATED: the resolved dimension is not COLLECTED (including TOOL_ABSENT, a refused or failed sshd -T, and every Standard Audit), or the setting is not reported exactly once. | PASS: the evidence is sufficient and the value is yes. The result concerns the global configuration. | FAIL: the evidence is sufficient and the value is no. | NOT_EVALUATED: the evidence is sufficient but the value is neither yes nor no. | never produced: NOT_APPLICABLE, MANUAL_REVIEW
limitations: sshd -T is run without a connection context; the result concerns the global configuration, and connection-specific state is not established by it. | Only the sshd at /usr/sbin/sshd is observed. | The permissions of individual home directories and key files are not evaluated here.

title: Every Command as Root Without Authentication
description: Every Command as Root Without Authentication: rules in the declared local sudo policy, as committed, that let a principal other than root run every command, as root, on every host, without authenticating. The conclusion concerns the declared policy only.
collection_requirements: FULL_AUDIT: /etc/sudoers and its includes are read only by a Full Audit (read_sudoers_graph_v1) | the route is necessary, not sufficient; evidence is sufficient when: | the coverage entry for /etc/sudoers with operation_id read_sudoers_graph_v1 has status COLLECTED | the sudo section is COLLECTED, its include_status is COLLECTED and its malformed_count is 0, with no UNSUPPORTED record
applicability: Every Linux host with a local sudo policy. This criterion never yields NOT_APPLICABLE: an /etc/sudoers that is not found gives NOT_EVALUATED, because the absence of sudo is not established by the absence of the file alone.
result_meanings: NOT_EVALUATED: the evidence is not sufficient: every Standard Audit, a refused or partial read, an unread include, an unsupported line, and an /etc/sudoers the Full Audit did not find (reason SUDOERS_ABSENT: with no declared policy to read, the absence of sudo is not established by this alone). | FAIL: the evidence is sufficient and some SPEC is decisive: its host is ALL (not negated); it runs as root (a run-as user list naming ALL or root, none negated or an alias, or no run-as list while runas_default is root: never set, or set only globally and only to root - sudoers(5): a rule without a run-as list runs as the runas_default user, root by default; when runas_default is set globally to another user, a rule without a run-as list is outside this criterion); it carries the command ALL, not negated, with NOPASSWD in force; no command in it is negated; and its principals - none negated, none an alias - include one that is not exactly the user root. A SPEC whose principals are only the user root is excluded. The result names each declaration with its file and line. | MANUAL_REVIEW: the evidence is sufficient, no SPEC is decisive, and some SPEC is an unresolved candidate: it carries NOPASSWD on ALL or on a command alias, runs as root or through a run-as alias or negation, concerns a principal other than only root, and an alias, a named or negated host, a negation, or a runas_default set in a user, host, run-as or command scope or to different values decides whether it grants every command as root without authentication. | PASS: the evidence is sufficient and no SPEC is decisive and none is an unresolved candidate: no declaration grants every command as root without authentication to a principal other than root, and no passwordless rule that could do so is left unresolved. | never produced: NOT_APPLICABLE
limitations: Declared policy only: sudo's last-match rule is not applied, so a FAIL states the declared grant, not sudo's decision for one user - a later rule may still require a password for that user. | A %group grant is reported for the group; its members are not resolved from the evidence. | NOPASSWD on a named list of commands is outside this criterion: it is not every command. | Defaults !authenticate, which removes the password for every rule in its scope, is ISE-PRIV-002. | Only the local sudo policy files are read; LDAP and SSSD sudo rules are not. | A host other than ALL is not matched against this host's name: such a rule is a MANUAL_REVIEW, never a FAIL. | When runas_default is never set, sudo's documented default, root, is taken; a sudo built with another compiled-in default is not detected (sudo -V shows it).

title: Authentication Disabled by sudo Defaults
description: Authentication Disabled by sudo Defaults: Defaults settings in the declared local sudo policy, as committed, that turn authentication off (!authenticate) for every rule or for a scope. The conclusion concerns the declared policy only.
collection_requirements: FULL_AUDIT: /etc/sudoers and its includes are read only by a Full Audit (read_sudoers_graph_v1) | the route is necessary, not sufficient; evidence is sufficient when: | the coverage entry for /etc/sudoers with operation_id read_sudoers_graph_v1 has status COLLECTED | the sudo section is COLLECTED, its include_status is COLLECTED and its malformed_count is 0, with no UNSUPPORTED record
applicability: Every Linux host with a local sudo policy. This criterion never yields NOT_APPLICABLE: an /etc/sudoers that is not found gives NOT_EVALUATED.
result_meanings: NOT_EVALUATED: the evidence is not sufficient: every Standard Audit, a refused or partial read, an unread include, an unsupported line, and an /etc/sudoers the Full Audit did not find (reason SUDOERS_ABSENT). | FAIL: the evidence is sufficient and some scope ends with !authenticate. A scope is identified by its type and one member as written (the global scope has one member; Defaults:alice,bob names the members alice and bob). Its settings are ordered by line within one file; settings of one scope in several files are ordered only when they agree, because the position of an include directive is not in the evidence. A scope whose member is an alias or a negation is never a FAIL. The result names each scope and its declarations. | MANUAL_REVIEW: the evidence is sufficient, no scope is a FAIL, and some scope is undecided: !authenticate set on a scope whose member is an alias or a negation, or settings of one scope that disagree and lie in several files. | PASS: the evidence is sufficient, no scope ends with !authenticate and none is undecided, including a policy that never sets authenticate. | never produced: NOT_APPLICABLE
limitations: Declared Defaults only. Scopes are compared as written: an alias used as a scope is not resolved, and a member written twice under different scopes of one type is compared as one member. | Precedence between scope types is not computed: a global !authenticate that a Defaults:alice authenticate re-enables for one user is still a FAIL for the global scope. | The order of settings in different files is not established from the evidence; settings that disagree across files give MANUAL_REVIEW. | rootpw, targetpw and runaspw are not assessed; NOPASSWD tags on rules are ISE-PRIV-001. | Only the local sudo policy files are read; LDAP and SSSD sudo rules are not.

title: Global SSH Root Login Setting
description: Global SSH Root Login Setting: the global value of PermitRootLogin that sshd -T reports, as committed. The conclusion concerns the global configuration only, not every connection.
collection_requirements: FULL_AUDIT: sshd -T is run only by a Full Audit (resolve_sshd_effective_config_v1) | the route is necessary, not sufficient; evidence is sufficient when: | the one coverage entry whose operation_id is resolve_sshd_effective_config_v1 has status COLLECTED | exactly one RESOLVED_SETTING record has keyword permitrootlogin
applicability: Every Linux host where the Full Audit ran sshd -T. Role-independent. This criterion never yields NOT_APPLICABLE.
result_meanings: NOT_EVALUATED: the resolved dimension is not COLLECTED (every Standard Audit, a refused or failed sshd -T), the setting is not reported exactly once, or its value is not one this criterion knows. | PASS: the evidence is sufficient and the value is no: root cannot log in over SSH by any method. | FAIL: the evidence is sufficient and the value is yes: root can log in over SSH with any enabled method, a password included. | MANUAL_REVIEW: the evidence is sufficient and the value is prohibit-password or its older name without-password (root can log in with a key or another method that is not a password), or forced-commands-only (root can log in only with a public key whose authorized_keys entry forces a command). The value sshd -T returned is reported unchanged, with what access remains. | never produced: NOT_APPLICABLE
limitations: Global effective configuration only: values that a Match block sets for some users, groups or addresses are not resolved, and a per-connection value may differ. | Whether root has a password or authorized keys at all is not part of this criterion; a FAIL states what the SSH daemon permits. | Under MANUAL_REVIEW, which keys or forced commands root accepts is in root's authorized_keys, which the Full Audit does not read today.

title: Global SSH Host-Based Authentication Disabled
description: Global SSH Host-Based Authentication Disabled: the global value of HostbasedAuthentication that sshd -T reports, as committed. The conclusion concerns the global configuration only.
collection_requirements: FULL_AUDIT: sshd -T is run only by a Full Audit (resolve_sshd_effective_config_v1) | the route is necessary, not sufficient; evidence is sufficient when: | the one coverage entry whose operation_id is resolve_sshd_effective_config_v1 has status COLLECTED | exactly one RESOLVED_SETTING record has keyword hostbasedauthentication
applicability: Every Linux host where the Full Audit ran sshd -T. Role-independent. This criterion never yields NOT_APPLICABLE.
result_meanings: NOT_EVALUATED: the resolved dimension is not COLLECTED (every Standard Audit, a refused or failed sshd -T), the setting is not reported exactly once, or its value is neither yes nor no. | PASS: the evidence is sufficient and the value is no: host-based authentication is off globally. | FAIL: the evidence is sufficient and the value is yes: the daemon accepts host-based authentication, a login vouched for by the connecting host. | never produced: NOT_APPLICABLE, MANUAL_REVIEW
limitations: Global effective configuration only: values that a Match block sets for some users, groups or addresses are not resolved, and a per-connection value may differ. | Which hosts are trusted (shosts.equiv, hosts.equiv, users' .rhosts and .shosts) is not read; ISE-SSH-005 concerns the users' files.

title: User Trust Files Ignored by SSH Host-Based Authentication
description: User Trust Files Ignored by SSH Host-Based Authentication: when host-based authentication is on globally, whether the global IgnoreRhosts that sshd -T reports, as committed, keeps users' own .rhosts and .shosts files from granting it. The conclusion concerns the global configuration only.
collection_requirements: FULL_AUDIT: sshd -T is run only by a Full Audit (resolve_sshd_effective_config_v1) | the route is necessary, not sufficient; evidence is sufficient when: | the one coverage entry whose operation_id is resolve_sshd_effective_config_v1 has status COLLECTED | exactly one RESOLVED_SETTING record has keyword hostbasedauthentication, and exactly one has keyword ignorerhosts
applicability: Hosts where the Full Audit ran sshd -T and HostbasedAuthentication is yes globally. NOT_APPLICABLE when it is no.
result_meanings: NOT_EVALUATED: the resolved dimension is not COLLECTED (every Standard Audit, a refused or failed sshd -T), a setting is not reported exactly once, or a value is not one this criterion knows. | NOT_APPLICABLE: the evidence is sufficient and HostbasedAuthentication is no: host-based authentication is off globally, so no user trust file can grant it (the documented condition of this criterion; ISE-SSH-004 reports the method itself). | PASS: the evidence is sufficient, HostbasedAuthentication is yes and IgnoreRhosts is yes: users' .rhosts and .shosts files are not used. | FAIL: the evidence is sufficient, HostbasedAuthentication is yes and IgnoreRhosts is no (users' .rhosts and .shosts files are used) or shosts-only (users' .shosts files are used). The result names the files that are allowed. | never produced: MANUAL_REVIEW
limitations: Global effective configuration only: values that a Match block sets for some users, groups or addresses are not resolved, and a per-connection value may differ. | The system-wide files /etc/hosts.equiv and /etc/ssh/shosts.equiv are outside this criterion: IgnoreRhosts does not govern them. | Whether any user actually has a .rhosts or .shosts file is not read.

title: /dev/shm Mounted nosuid
description: /dev/shm Mounted nosuid: whether the active mount at /dev/shm in the host's mount table, as committed, carries the nosuid option. The conclusion concerns that mount only.
collection_requirements: FULL_AUDIT: only a Full Audit reads the host's mount table (/proc/1/mountinfo); a Standard Audit reads its own process's view and cannot establish the host's namespace | the route is necessary, not sufficient; evidence is sufficient when: | the active side of the mounts section is COLLECTED and complete | every active mount record was read from /proc/1/mountinfo (the host's mount namespace) | exactly one active mount has the mount point /dev/shm, and its line was parsed
applicability: Every Linux host whose Full Audit read the host's mount table. Role-independent. This criterion never yields NOT_APPLICABLE.
result_meanings: NOT_EVALUATED: the evidence is not sufficient: an incomplete or uncollected active table, a table that is not the host's (every Standard Audit), no mount at /dev/shm, more than one mount at /dev/shm, or an unparsed mount line. | PASS: the evidence is sufficient and the /dev/shm mount carries nosuid. | FAIL: the evidence is sufficient and the /dev/shm mount does not carry nosuid. The result shows the mount point and the options observed. | never produced: NOT_APPLICABLE, MANUAL_REVIEW
limitations: The host's mount namespace only (PID 1's): containers and other mount namespaces are not observed. | Other options of /dev/shm (nodev, noexec) and other world-writable mounts (/tmp, /var/tmp) are outside this criterion. | The options in effect at collection time; a later remount is not seen.
